sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he knows that Antwerp is the greatest prize of all, because as you said, it's probably the richest city, certainly in Europe, I mean, maybe in the world.
sentences.zh: 他知道安特卫普是最重大的奖赏，因为正如你所说，它可能是最富有的城市，当然在欧洲是这样，我的意思是，也许在全世界也是如此。

sentences.en: And it is the key Protestant stronghold.
sentences.zh: 它是主要的抗争新教堡垒。

sentences.en: This is where Protestantism is strongeSt. And if he can take Antwerp, then he's probably thinking that is the end of the revolt.
sentences.zh: 这里是新教势力最强大的地方。如果他能攻克安特卫普，那么他可能会认为起义就此结束了。

sentences.en: So he had embarked on the siege of Antwerp in June 1584, and he constructed an immense network of forts to cut off Antwerp's access to the interior of the southern low countries.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在1584年6月开始了对安特卫普的围攻，并修建了一个庞大的堡垒网络，以切断安特卫普与低地国家南部内陆的联系。

sentences.en: But the key requirement is to stop supplies and men from the rebel-held north reaching the city down the Shelt, this kind of great estuary which leads out into the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 但关键的要求是阻止来自叛军控制的北方的物资和人员顺着斯海尔德河——这条通往北海的巨大河口——到达该市。

sentences.en: And Parma achieves this by building a massive pontoon bridge, which his admirers are very proud of saying was twice the length of the bridge built by Julius Caesar over the Rhine.
sentences.zh: 帕尔马通过建造一座巨大的浮桥实现了这一点，他的崇拜者非常自豪地称，这座桥的长度是尤利乌斯·恺撒建造的莱茵河桥的两倍。

sentences.en: So it's almost half a mile in length.
sentences.zh: 所以它的长度将近半英里。

sentences.en: And the rebels are so desperate to destroy it that they send in fireships, hell burners, they're called, loaded with explosives to blow it up.
sentences.zh: 叛军迫切想要摧毁它，以至于派出了火船——被称为地狱烧船——装满炸药去炸毁它。

sentences.en: And actually one of these fireships does blow up and it incinerates an entire section of the bridge, killing 800 Spanish soldiers.
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中一艘火船确实爆炸了，将桥梁的一整段化为灰烬，炸死了800名西班牙士兵。

sentences.en: But Parma is able to have it repaired before the Dutch rebels can come down and force their way through the gap that they've opened up.
sentences.zh: 但荷兰叛军还没来得及顺流而下并从他们打开的缺口强行突围之前，帕尔马就把它修好了。

sentences.en: And so in late May, the rebels try again, but this time their fleet makes a complete hash of things.
sentences.zh: 因此在5月下旬，叛军再次尝试，但这一次他们的舰队把事情彻底搞砸了。

sentences.en: The tide turns and sweeps them back towards their own lines, which is not that you want to see a load of fireships loaded with explosives coming towards you on a tide.
sentences.zh: 潮水转向，将他们冲回了自己的防线，这可不是你想看到的——一堆装满炸药的火船顺着潮水向你冲来。

sentences.en: And again, Parma is able to repel the attack and to maintain the integrity of the pontoon bridge across the Shelt.
sentences.zh: 帕尔马再次击退了进攻，并保持了横跨斯海尔德河的浮桥的完整性。

sentences.en: And this means that Antwerp is now completely invested.
sentences.zh: 这意味着安特卫普现在被彻底围困了。

sentences.en: And so starvation starts to grip the city and the rebels grow increasingly desperate.
sentences.zh: 因此饥饿开始笼罩这座城市，叛军也变得越来越绝望。

sentences.en: And they are looking around for allies.
sentences.zh: 他们开始四处寻找盟友。

sentences.en: They need overseas support, but where are they going to get this support from?
sentences.zh: 他们需要海外支持，但他们能从哪里获得这种支持呢？

sentences.en: So in the previous episode, we talked about how the rebels had tried to get French backing in the form of Anjou, the duke who had been hoping to marry
sentences.zh: 所以在上一集中，我们讨论了叛军如何试图获得法国的支持，即阿茹，这位曾希望迎娶

sentences.en: Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白的公爵。

sentences.en: But he had hashed things up.
sentences.zh: 但他把事情搞砸了。

sentences.en: His mercenaries had run amok in Antwerp.
sentences.zh: 他的雇佣兵在安特卫普大肆胡闹。

sentences.en: He'd left in disgrace and now he's dead.
sentences.zh: 他在耻辱中离开，现在他已经死了。

sentences.en: And so the rebels have tried to get his brother, Henry III of France to take over the sovereignty of the low countries and come in against Spain.
sentences.zh: 因此，叛军试图让他的兄弟、法国国王亨利三世接管低地国家的主权并加入反对西班牙的阵营。

sentences.en: But as we've said,
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所说，

sentences.en: Henry III is the king of a country that is now collapsing into civil war.
sentences.zh: 亨利三世是一个正陷入内战的国家的国王。

sentences.en: So he doesn't have time to intervene in foreign squabbles.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有时间干涉外国的纷争。

sentences.en: And this really leaves the rebels with just the one port of call.
sentences.zh: 这实际上让叛军只有一个求助对象。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is a queen who is, as we've said, instinctively cautious, hates spending money on wars, hates wars full stop, very much disapproves of revolts against
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是那个正如我们所说的那样，天生谨慎、讨厌在战争上花钱、彻底讨厌战争、非常反对反抗

sentences.en: anointed monarchs.
sentences.zh: 受膏君主的英国女王。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is Elizabeth of England.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是英国的伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: And so unsurprisingly, when the Dutch rebels go to London and offer her sovereignty over the low countries, she turns them down.
sentences.zh: 因此，当荷兰叛军前往伦敦并向她提供低地国家的主权时，她拒绝了他们，这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: However, she and her government do appreciate that they can't really just leave the rebels to the fate.
sentences.zh: 然而，她和她的政府确实意识到，他们不能真的就这样把叛军听天由命。

sentences.en: It is existential for England as well as for the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 这对英国和荷兰来说都是生死攸关的事。

sentences.en: And in particular, the impending fall of Antwerp is a nightmare for English strategists.
sentences.zh: 特别是，安特卫普即将陷落对英国战略家来说是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: First of all, it risks the collapse of the entire Dutch revolt.
sentences.zh: 首先，这有可能导致整个荷兰起义的崩溃。

sentences.en: And if the Dutch revolt collapses, then, as we've said, that means that Palmer and his terrifying army will be free to cross the sea and land in
sentences.zh: 如果荷兰起义崩溃，那么正如我们所说，这意味着帕尔马和他可怕的军队将可以自由地跨海并在

sentences.en: England.
sentences.zh: 英国登陆。

sentences.en: More broadly, it's a nightmare for the entire cause of Protestantism in Europe.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，这对欧洲整个新教事业来说是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: And for
sentences.zh: 对于

sentences.en: Leicester, for Walsingham, for Sydney, definitely.
sentences.zh: 莱斯特、沃尔辛厄姆、西德尼来说，绝对如此。

sentences.en: This is probably the major consideration.
sentences.zh: 这可能是最主要的考量。

sentences.en: You know, this is the future of what God wants for Christendom is at stake as they see it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如他们所看到的，上帝对基督教世界的未来愿景正处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And what about the economics of it?
sentences.zh: 那经济方面呢？

sentences.en: Because you mentioned how wealthy the Flemish cloth towns are, how important that trade link is between the low countries and
sentences.zh: 因为你提到了法兰德斯呢绒城镇是多么富有，低地国家与

sentences.en: England in particular.
sentences.zh: 英国之间的贸易联系是多么重要。

sentences.en: I mean, surely if Antwerp was lost, if the low countries were lost, wouldn't that be disastrous for England's economy?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果安特卫普失守，如果低地国家失守，那对英国经济来说难道不是灾难性的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, a complete disaster.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: I mean, there've been blockades going on and off throughout this period.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这期间一直断断续续地有封锁。

sentences.en: But the thought of losing Antwerp, the kind of Straits of Hormuz cubed, basically, for the
sentences.zh: 但想到失去安特卫普——基本上就是

sentences.en: English.
sentences.zh: 英国人的霍尔木兹海峡平方。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a massive, massive disaster.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一场极其巨大的灾难。

sentences.en: They cannot afford to have Antwerp under the control of a hostile power.
sentences.zh: 他们承担不起让安特卫普处于敌对势力控制之下的后果。

sentences.en: And it is clear to them by now that Philip II is indeed an overtly hostile power who is looking to throttle the entire English economy.
sentences.zh: 他们现在已经清楚，腓力二世确实是一个公开敌对的势力，正试图扼杀整个英国经济。

sentences.en: Because back in May 1585, he'd imposed an embargo on English vessels landing in Spanish and Portuguese ports.
sentences.zh: 因为早在1585年5月，他就对停泊在西班牙和葡萄牙港口的英国船只实施了禁运。

sentences.en: And this is a patent act of economic warfare.
sentences.zh: 这是一个明显的经济战行为。

sentences.en: And so the prospect that he might end up in a position to impose a similar embargo on all the ports in the low countries, I mean, that is a complete nightmare.
sentences.zh: 因此，他最终可能会处于对低地国家所有港口实施类似禁运的地位，这种前景——我的意思是，这是一场彻底的噩梦。

sentences.en: And it's the kind of nightmare that Elizabeth, who's always counting the pennies, that she can actually understand.
sentences.zh: 这也是伊丽莎白这种总是锱铢必较的人能够真正理解的噩梦。

sentences.en: You know, she's less interested in glory than she is in making money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她对荣耀的兴趣不如对赚钱的兴趣大。

sentences.en: And this is enough to make her think, well, probably we should do something about this.
sentences.zh: 这就足以让她认为，好吧，我们也许应该为此做点什么。

sentences.en: And so by early August
sentences.zh: 因此，到1585年

sentences.en: 1585, it's clear that Antwerp isn't going to hold out much longer.
sentences.zh: 8月初，很明显安特卫普撑不了多久了。

sentences.en: You know, they're thinking in terms of weeks, maybe days before the Spanish enter the city.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们觉得以周为单位，甚至可能几天内西班牙人就要进城了。

sentences.en: And that means that Elizabeth, who,
sentences.zh: 这意味着伊丽莎白，这个...

sentences.en: given the choice, will always delay and prevaricate.
sentences.zh: 只要有得选，就总是会拖延和敷衍的人。

sentences.en: It means that she has to arrive at a decision about what to do.
sentences.zh: 意味着她必须就该怎么做做出决定。

sentences.en: And of course, much is going to depend on that decision, the course of the Dutch revolt, the prospects of open war between England and Spain, and the future officer Philip Sidney.
sentences.zh: 当然，许多事情都将取决于这个决定：荷兰起义的进程、英西两国爆发公开战争的前景，以及未来的军官菲利普·西德尼。

sentences.en: Oh, that's exciting.
sentences.zh: 噢，那可太让人兴奋了。

sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫里的那个家伙在玩火，亚历克斯。

sentences.zh: 我们需要了解政策背景。

sentences.en: Tom, throughout history, change has often been driven by businesses and institutions that end up having a massive impact on society as a whole.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，纵观历史，变革往往是由那些最终对整个社会产生巨大影响的企业和机构推动的。

sentences.en: And there's probably no better example than the Ford Motor Company.
sentences.zh: 而最好的例子莫过于福特汽车公司了。

sentences.en: Henry Ford and his managers revolutionised production through their pioneering assembly lines.
sentences.zh: 亨利·福特和他的管理者们通过开创性的装配线彻底革新了生产方式。

sentences.en: And they influenced factories and working practices in countries all over the world.
sentences.zh: 他们影响了世界各地工厂和工作实践。

sentences.en: Another example of a business driving technological and social change is Amazon, which is increasing the number of its electric vehicles used for deliveries in Europe
sentences.zh: 另一个推动技术和社会变革的企业的例子是亚马逊，该公司正在增加其在欧洲用于配送的电动汽车数量，

sentences.en: to over 10,000 by the end of this year, 2026.
sentences.zh: 计划在今年（2026年）底前超过10,000辆。

sentences.en: Now, on top of that, over 50% of Amazon deliveries now come with less packaging, or sometimes no added packaging at all.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，现在超过50%的亚马逊配送包裹都采用更少的包装，有时甚至完全不添加额外包装。

sentences.en: It helps to avoid unnecessary waste and it makes recycling at home that much easier.
sentences.zh: 这有助于避免不必要的浪费，并大大简化了家中的回收利用。

sentences.en: Find out more at amazon.co.uk slash sustainability.
sentences.zh: 访问 amazon.co.uk slash sustainability 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的沉淀》。

sentences.en: We return with bombshell news from Antwerp, because it's the 17th of August, 1585.
sentences.zh: 我们带着来自安特卫普的重磅新闻回归，因为今天是1585年8月17日。

sentences.en: And after a siege of 13 months, the richest city in this part of Europe, perhaps in all Europe, has finally surrendered to the Prince of Parma.
sentences.zh: 经过13个月的围城，欧洲这一地区、或许甚至是整个欧洲最富有的城市，终于向帕尔马亲王投降了。

sentences.en: Actually, the end of the siege is not quite as bloody and gory as you might expect.
sentences.zh: 其实，围城的结局并没有你想象的那么血腥和残忍。

sentences.en: So, the Spanish are very well behaved, aren't they, in victory.
sentences.zh: 所以，西班牙人在胜利时的表现相当不错，对吧？

sentences.en: And the terms, you said in the first half, Tom, that the terms that Parma offers his defeated adversaries are often pretty generous, and they are in this case, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 而关于条款，汤姆，你刚才在前半段说过，帕尔马给战败对手的条款通常都相当慷慨，这次也是这样，对吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Antwerp, which had been the great stronghold of Protestantism in the Low Countries, is formally restored to Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 因此，曾是低地国家新教大本营的安特卫普，正式恢复了天主教。

sentences.en: But, as with Ghentz, so in Antwerp, Protestants are allowed to leave the city if they want.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如根特一样，在安特卫普，新教徒如果愿意，也可以离开这座城市。

sentences.en: And huge numbers do so.
sentences.zh: 大量的人确实这么做了。

sentences.en: So, probably around 60,000 people out of a total population of 100,000, so more than half.
sentences.zh: 因此，大约有60,000人离开了这座总人口100,000的城市，超过了一半。

sentences.en: And this is actually a disaster for Antwerp, because most of the people who are leaving, lots of them are bankers, merchants, the cutting edge of capitalism.
sentences.zh: 这对安特卫普来说实际上是一场灾难，因为离开的大多数人都是银行家、商人和资本主义的尖兵。

sentences.en: And most of them head northwards to Holland, which is still the great nerve centre of the Dutch revolt.
sentences.zh: 他们大部分向北前往荷兰，那里依然是荷兰起义的巨大神经中枢。

sentences.en: And there they settle, lots of them, in a kind of new upstart hotspot for business.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里定居，许多人来到了一个可以说是新兴的商业热点城市。

sentences.en: And this is a city called Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 这座城市名叫阿姆斯特丹。

sentences.en: And so, the arrival of these exiles from Antwerp is really the making of Amsterdam as the great city of 17th century capitalism.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些来自安特卫普的流亡者的到来，真正造就了阿姆斯特丹作为17世纪资本主义伟大城市的地位。

sentences.en: Our Dutch listeners will be pleased to be reminded that they basically owe their prominence and prosperity to the Belgians.
sentences.zh: 我们的荷兰听众会很高兴听到有人提醒他们，他们的大部分声望和繁荣其实都要归功于比利时人。

sentences.en: So, Antwerp has fallen, and in England, great gloom and foreboding, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，安特卫普陷落了，英国上下则是一片阴霾与不祥的预感，对吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, this is terrible, terrible news.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是个极其糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: And so, three days later, after the fall of Antwerp on the 20th of August,
sentences.zh: 因此，在安特卫普陷落三天后的8月20日，

sentences.en: a treaty is signed between Elizabeth I and the Dutch rebels at a palace built by Henry VIII at a place called Nonsuch in Surrey.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白一世与荷兰起义军在萨里郡的“无双宫”（亨利八世建造的一座宫殿）签署了一项条约。

sentences.en: And this is the first ever treaty signed by what will become the Dutch Republic with a foreign power.
sentences.zh: 这是日后将成为荷兰共和国的国家与外国签署的第一份条约。

sentences.en: And by its terms, Elizabeth agrees to send an expeditionary force to the Low Countries to support Holland and the other rebel provinces.
sentences.zh: 根据条约条款，伊丽莎白同意向低地国家派遣一支远征军，以支持荷兰及其他起义省份。

sentences.en: And this is to consist of 6,350 infantry and 1,000 cavalry.
sentences.zh: 这支部队将由6,350名步兵和1,000名骑兵组成。

sentences.en: And amazingly, Elizabeth says, I will subsidise the cost of this.
sentences.zh: 令人惊叹的是，伊丽莎白表示，我将资助这笔费用。

sentences.en: I mean, it must have caused her agony to do that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这么做一定让她感到痛苦万分。

sentences.en: And she chooses, as the commander of this expeditionary force, her old favourite, the Earl of Leicester.
sentences.zh: 她选择她的老情人莱斯特伯爵担任这支远征军的指挥官。

sentences.en: And because she doesn't entirely trust the Dutch, she obliges them to hand over three key ports to English garrisons to serve the English as what are described as cautionary towns.
sentences.zh: 由于她并非完全信任荷兰人，她强迫他们将三个关键港口交由英国守军控制，作为英国所谓的“警戒城镇”。

sentences.en: So, basically, these towns are kind of hostages.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，这些城镇就像是人质。

sentences.en: And they are the town of Brill, which commanded the mouth of the Great River Mars, or the Meurs, if you're speaking in French.
sentences.zh: 它们是布里尔镇，该镇控制着马斯河（如果说法语则是默兹河）大河的河口；

sentences.en: And Flushing and Rameken, which are ports on an island just beyond the Scheldt Estuary.
sentences.zh: 还有法兰盛和拉梅肯，这两个港口位于斯海尔德河口外的一个岛屿上。

sentences.en: And the reason for choosing these ports is that between them, it enables the English to control what goes in and goes out of the Scheldt Estuary down towards Antwerp.
sentences.zh: 选择这些港口的原因是，它们结合起来能让英国人控制进出斯海尔德河口并顺流而下前往安特卫普的船只。

sentences.en: So, in other words, to throttle the ability of the Spanish to move by sea from Antwerp round the northern coast towards the rebel heartlands in Holland and Zeeland.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是扼杀西班牙人通过海路由安特卫普绕过北部海岸前往荷兰和西兰起义核心腹地的能力。

sentences.en: And the guy who's going to be in charge of one of these, Flushing, is the star of today's episode.
sentences.zh: 而将负责其中一个港口（法兰盛）的人，正是今天这集的主角。

sentences.en: He's finally got his chance.
sentences.zh: 他终于迎来了自己的机会。

sentences.en: He's finally got his opportunity to have a crack at the Spanish and write his name into the history books.
sentences.zh: 他终于有机会跟西班牙人较量一番，并将自己的名字载入史册。

sentences.en: And that is our friend Sir Philip Sidney.
sentences.zh: 他就是我们的朋友菲利普·西德尼爵士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, hooray for Sir Philip Sidney.
sentences.zh: 所以，为菲利普·西德尼爵士欢呼吧。

sentences.en: And I think he owes this appointment to various factors.
sentences.zh: 我认为他能得到这个任命归因于多种因素。

sentences.en: Favouritism, obviously.
sentences.zh: 当然是因为裙带关系。

sentences.en: He's the nephew of Leicester, who has been appointed to the command of this expedition.
sentences.zh: 他是莱斯特的侄子，而莱斯特已被任命为这次远征的指挥官。

sentences.en: He's put in a lot of hard work preparing the Treaty of Nonsuch.
sentences.zh: 他在筹备《无双宫条约》时付出了大量艰苦的努力。

sentences.en: Basically, he'd spent all summer at the palace kind of oiling the wheels.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他整个夏天都在宫里上下打点、穿针引线。

sentences.en: And the Dutch envoys had absolutely loved him.
sentences.zh: 荷兰特使们对他是极其喜爱。

sentences.en: So, they had saluted his wisdom, kindness and his other gifts.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们对他的智慧、善良和其他天赋赞不绝口。

sentences.en: So, it's all looking good for Sidney.
sentences.zh: 所以，西德尼的前景一片大好。

sentences.en: But then, in classic Elizabeth I style, she starts to wobble.
sentences.zh: 但随后，带着典型的伊丽莎白一世风格，她开始动摇了。

sentences.en: First of all, she hesitates over whether she actually wants Leicester as governor general.
sentences.zh: 首先，她犹豫着是否真的想要莱斯特担任总督。

sentences.en: Does she really want him going to the low countries?
sentences.zh: 她真的想让他去低地国家吗？

sentences.en: And then, to Sidney's absolute fury, she tells him, I don't want you going to Flushing after all.
sentences.zh: 紧接着，在西德尼暴怒之下，她告诉他：“我最终还是不希望你去法兰盛。”

sentences.en: She's changed her mind.
sentences.zh: 她改变主意了。

sentences.en: And so, he has the most massive strop.
sentences.zh: 于是他大发雷霆。

sentences.en: He storms off, he gets on his horse, and he gallops off to Plymouth.
sentences.zh: 他气冲冲地离开，骑上马，一路狂奔到普利茅斯。

sentences.en: And the reason he goes to Plymouth is because Sidney knows that the low countries aren't the only place where there might be a chance for him to win glory for himself.
sentences.zh: 他去普利茅斯的原因是西德尼知道，低地国家并不是唯一一个能让他赢得个人荣耀的地方。

sentences.en: There are other opportunities for would-be dashing young adventurers because all summer, when he wasn't negotiating with Dutch diplomats,
sentences.zh: 对于那些渴望成为风流倜傥的年轻冒险家来说，还有其他机会，因为整个夏天，当他不与荷兰外交官谈判时，

sentences.en: Sidney had been helping Sir Francis Drake prepare for a massive expedition to the Indies.
sentences.zh: 西德尼一直在协助弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士筹备前往西印度群岛的大规模远征。

sentences.en: And when I say massive, I mean it is the largest English fleet that has been raised for over a century.
sentences.zh: 当我说是大规模时，我是说这是了一个多世纪以来组建的最大规模的英国舰队。

sentences.en: So, some 20 ships, two of them provided by Elizabeth herself, including Drake's flagship, the Elizabeth Bonaventura.
sentences.zh: 大约20艘船，其中两艘由伊丽莎白本人提供，包括德雷克的旗舰“伊丽莎白·博纳文图拉号”。

sentences.en: And the plan, which has been drawn up by Drake, by the Privy Council, by Elizabeth herself, is for Drake to plunder as much gold and silver from the Spanish as he possibly can,
sentences.zh: 这个由德雷克、枢密院以及伊丽莎白本人制定的计划是，由德雷克尽可能多地掠夺西班牙人的金银，

sentences.en: and then use the proceeds to help fund the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 然后用这些收益来资助荷兰人。

sentences.en: So, just as Philip has been targeting the English economy, the plan is that Drake will target the infrastructure that sustains Philip's supply of treasure.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如腓力一直在针对英国经济一样，该计划是德雷克将目标对准维持腓力财富供应的基础设施。

sentences.en: And Lord Burley, who previously had been a bit of a Drake skeptic, I mean, he's right behind this.
sentences.zh: 而以前对德雷克持怀疑态度的伯利勋爵，现在可以说是坚决支持。

sentences.en: He thinks this is a brilliant plan.
sentences.zh: 他认为这是一个绝妙的计划。

sentences.en: And so, he'd written to Walsingham about Philip, Philip II.
sentences.zh: 因此，他曾就腓力二世写信给沃尔辛厄姆：

sentences.en: Whilst his riches of the Indies continue, he thinketh he will be able with them to weary out all other princes.
sentences.zh: “只要西印度群岛的财富还在源源不断，他认为自己就能用它们来拖垮所有其他的君主。”

sentences.en: Those taken away himself will quickly fall.
sentences.zh: “一旦这些被夺走，他自己也将迅速垮台。”

sentences.en: And I know by good means that he more feareth this action of Sir Francis than he ever did anything that hath been attempted against him.
sentences.zh: “而且我通过可靠途径得知，他比以往对付过他的任何行动都更害怕弗朗西斯的这一举动。”

sentences.en: So, really interesting illustration of the sensitivity of people in the 16th century to the opportunities provided by economic warfare.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的例证，说明了16世纪的人们对经济战所带来的机遇是多么敏感。

sentences.en: I think people are kind of becoming more and more alert to this.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对这一点的警惕性越来越高。

sentences.en: So, Sidney must be terribly excited about this.
sentences.zh: 所以西德尼对此肯定兴奋极了。

sentences.en: I mean, this really is a tremendous chance to win the kind of glory that he's been after.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实是一个绝佳的机会，能赢得他一直追求的那种荣耀。

sentences.en: And when Drake's fleet sails out of Plymouth on the 14th of September, Drake is on the flagship and Sidney is there with him.
sentences.zh: 当德雷克的舰队于9月14日驶离普利茅斯时，德雷克在旗舰上，西德尼也和他在一起。

sentences.en: I mean, it's potentially one of the great double acts in English history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这潜在地可能是英国历史上最伟大的双人组合之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, one of the great kind of buddy acts.
sentences.zh: 对，某种最棒的搭档组合之一。

sentences.en: But it doesn't happen because just as they're pulling out of Plymouth Sound in the Bonaventura,
sentences.zh: 但这并没有发生，因为就在他们乘坐“博纳文图拉号”驶出普利茅斯湾时，

sentences.en: a rowing boat comes up the side of the boat with a message from the Queen and she's changed her mind.
sentences.zh: 一艘划艇靠近了他们的船，带来了女王的口信，她改变主意了。

sentences.en: And actually, she does want Sidney to go to Flushing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她确实希望西德尼去法兰盛。

sentences.en: And so, Sidney gets off the boat, gets into the rowing boat and goes back to London and ultimately to Flushing.
sentences.zh: 于是西德尼下了船，坐上划艇返回伦敦，最终去了法兰盛。

sentences.en: And obviously, Elizabeth is furious with Sidney.
sentences.zh: 显然，伊丽莎白对西德尼大发雷霆。

sentences.en: I mean, she doesn't like people rushing off without telling her.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她不喜欢别人不打招呼就擅自跑掉。

sentences.en: But she can't come down too hard on him because I think she has realised in his absence that actually, much to her annoyance, she does need him.
sentences.zh: 但她又不能对他太严厉，因为我想她在他离开期间已经意识到，尽管她很不高兴，但她确实需要他。

sentences.en: So, Leicester, who she has by this point reappointed as Governor General of the Low Countries,
sentences.zh: 所以，莱斯特（此时她已重新任命他为低地国家总督）

sentences.en: he's busy recruiting troops around England and Wales and so won't be able to leave for the Low Countries until December.
sentences.zh: 正忙着在英格兰和威尔士各地招募军队，因此直到12月才能离开前往低地国家。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Palmer isn't waiting.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，帕尔马并没有闲着。

sentences.en: He's advancing on all fronts and the Dutch desperately need English support.
sentences.zh: 他全线推进，荷兰人迫切需要英国的支持。

sentences.en: And everyone, the Dutch, the English alike, are agreed there is only the one man for the job.
sentences.zh: 每个人——无论是荷兰人还是英国人都一致认为，只有一个人能胜任这个工作。

sentences.en: It has to be Sir Philip Sidney.
sentences.zh: 非菲利普·西德尼爵士莫属。

sentences.en: And so, Sidney goes to the Low Countries, which, as you said, Dominic, means that he misses his chance to go on an expedition to the New World, which he had, as you said,
sentences.zh: 因此，西德尼去了低地国家，正如你所说的那门，多米尼克，这意味着他错去了前往新世界的远征机会，正如你所说，

sentences.en: been very, very excited about.
sentences.zh: 他对此曾感到非常非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And so, just to give a quick resume of the excitements he misses before we come to what Sidney gets up to in the Low Countries.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们讲到西德尼在低地国家的所作所为之前，先简单回顾一下他错过的那些惊险刺激。

sentences.en: I mean, Drake heads southwards and he has the most lovely time.
sentences.zh: 德雷克向南航行，过得那叫一个愉快。

sentences.en: So, he turns up in Spain and he extorts supplies out of a town in Galicia in northern Spain called Vigo and he stays there for two weeks.
sentences.zh: 他出现在西班牙，从西班牙北部加利西亚的一个叫维哥的城镇勒索了补给物资，并在那里逗留了两周。

sentences.en: And it's seen by Philip, I think quite correctly,
sentences.zh: 腓力认为这绝对是一个巨大的羞辱，我认为他的看法完全正确，

sentences.en: as an absolutely massive humiliation that this English pirate has turned up and kind of replenished his supplies from Spanish stocks.
sentences.zh: 这个英国海盗竟然出现，并用西班牙的库存来补充自己的物资。

sentences.en: Then Drake sweeps across the Atlantic, capturing and plundering Spanish strongholds as he goes.
sentences.zh: 随后，德雷克横渡大西洋，一路攻占并掠夺了西班牙的据点。

sentences.en: And when Drake captures Santo Domingo in what is now the Dominican Republic, he's waiting for the ransom and to force the Spanish to hurry up.
sentences.zh: 当德雷克攻占了现今多米尼加共和国境内的圣多明各时，他一边等待赎金，为了迫使西班牙人快点，

sentences.en: He starts literally disassembling the city brick by brick until they've brought the gold.
sentences.zh: 他甚至开始一砖一瓦地拆卸这座城市，直到他们把黄金送来。

sentences.en: And then, you know, he's got the ransom and then it's on to Cartagena in Colombia, which he also captures.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，他拿到了赎金，接着前往哥伦比亚的卡塔赫纳，他也攻占了那里。

sentences.en: Again, he extorts a massive ransom.
sentences.zh: 同样，他勒索了巨额赎金。

sentences.en: And this isn't a long expedition.
sentences.zh: 这不是一次漫长的远征。

sentences.en: He's back in Plymouth by the 22nd of July, 1586.
sentences.zh: 他在1586年7月22日之前就回到了普利茅斯。

sentences.en: And actually, it's not quite as lucrative as Drake had been hoping.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这并没有德雷克希望的那么赚。

sentences.en: He doesn't manage to capture any treasure ships.
sentences.zh: 他没能截获任何装载财宝的船只。

sentences.en: But strategically, it is hugely significant because as he'd done before, he's able to highlight the pretty precarious nature of Spain's American empire.
sentences.zh: 但在战略上，它具有极其重大的意义，因为正如他以前所做的那样，他得以突显出西班牙美洲帝国相当脆弱的本质。

sentences.en: And the result of this in Europe is to undermine Philip's credit with his bankers.
sentences.zh: 这在欧洲产生的结果是削弱了腓力在银行家心目中的信誉。

sentences.en: And so the Pope and the Dukes of Florence and Savoy all refuse him alone when the news of Drake's expedition reaches them.
sentences.zh: 因此，当德雷克远征的消息传到教皇以及佛罗伦萨和萨伏依公爵耳中时，他们都拒绝借钱给他。

sentences.en: And the Bank of Seville actually goes buSt.
sentences.zh: 塞维利亚银行甚至直接破产了。

sentences.en: And Burley is kind of cackling and rubbing his hands at this and says, truly, Sir Francis Drake is a fearful man to the king of Spain, which I think he is.
sentences.zh: 而伯利在一旁咯咯笑着，搓着手说道，弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士对西班牙国王来说真是一个令人畏惧的人，我也深以为然。

sentences.en: So, while Drake's been off sacking Cartagena and whatnot, what has Sir Philip Sidney doing?
sentences.zh: 那么，当德雷克跑去洗劫卡塔赫纳等地时，菲利普·西德尼爵士在做什么呢？

sentences.en: Because he's been in the slightly more unglamorous surroundings of flushing on the...
sentences.zh: 因为他一直身处弗利辛恩那些多少有些不够光鲜亮丽的环境中……

sentences.en: Yeah, an island off the Scheldt estuary.
sentences.zh: 对，那是斯海尔德河口附近的一个岛屿。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's arrived there in mid-November, which is never really a great time to turn up to an island in the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以他在11月中旬抵达了那里，对于去北海的一个岛屿来说，这绝不是一个好时机。

sentences.en: It's completely miserable.
sentences.zh: 那里简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And when he lands, he has to walk three miles through mud before he can reach the port itself.
sentences.zh: 他一登陆，就必须在泥地里走三英里才能到达港口本身。

sentences.en: And he wrote to Leicester, as dirty a walk as ever, poor governor entered his charge with all.
sentences.zh: 他写信给莱斯特，这也是可怜的总督上任以来最泥泞的一次步行。

sentences.en: Leicester himself arrives in Flushing three weeks later, and he's greeted there by Sidney, by the two sons of William the Silent, and by bonfires made, and I quote,
sentences.zh: 莱斯特本人在三周后抵达了弗利辛恩，西德尼、沉默者威廉的两个儿子以及点燃的篝火在那里迎接了他，我引用一下：

sentences.en: after the Dutch manor, which is to fix great pitch barrels on the tops of high poles and then to fire them.
sentences.zh: 按照荷兰人的习俗，就是在高高的木杆顶上固定巨大的沥青桶，然后将其点燃。

sentences.en: So, Leicester has a better arrival than Sidney had done, and the pair of them then head off in triumphal manner via Delft to the Hague,
sentences.zh: 所以，莱斯特的抵达比西德尼要风光，随后两人经代尔夫特以凯旋般的方式前往海牙，

sentences.en: where Leicester then leaves Sidney to finalise the precise details of his role and status in the Low Countries.
sentences.zh: 莱斯特在那里留下西德尼，去敲定他在低地国家扮演的角色和身份的具体细节。

sentences.en: And Sidney's very ambitious for his uncle, and he goes well beyond the governor's rebate, and he secures a post for Leicester,
sentences.zh: 西德尼为他的叔叔抱负远大，他的行事超出了总督权限的范围，他为莱斯特争取到一个职位，

sentences.en: which implies that Elizabeth is in fact sovereign over the Low Countries, which is exactly what Elizabeth had not wanted him to do.
sentences.zh: 这暗示伊丽莎白事实上对低地国家拥有主权，而这正是伊丽莎白最不想让他做的事情。

sentences.en: And I think the reason that Sidney does this is that he's aware that Leicester needs to seem as prestigious to the Dutch rebels and indeed to the Spanish as possible if he's going to be able to play an effective role in the coming war.
sentences.zh: 我想西德尼之所以这么做，是因为他意识到，如果莱斯特想在即将到来的战争中发挥有效作用，就必须在荷兰叛军甚至西班牙人面前显得尽可能具有崇高的威望。

sentences.en: But obviously, when Elizabeth gets the news, she is furious, and they have a massive row, and I think for the Dutch,
sentences.zh: 但很显然，当伊丽莎白得知这个消息时，她勃然大怒，他们大吵了一架，我想对于荷兰人来说，

sentences.en: it's a bit like watching mummy and daddy have a kind of quarrel.
sentences.zh: 这有点像看着爸爸妈妈在吵架。

sentences.en: It's very awkward for all concerned.
sentences.zh: 这对所有相关的人来说都非常尴尬。

sentences.en: And from this point on, essentially, everything goes downhill for Leicester, because it turns out that his qualities, amazingly, he's a very arrogant aristocrat,
sentences.zh: 从这一刻起，基本上莱斯特的一切都开始走下坡路，因为事实证明，他那些惊人的品质——他是个非常傲慢的贵族，

sentences.en: turn out not to be those of a natural diplomat.
sentences.zh: 证明了他并不是一个天生的外交官。

sentences.en: So he's very, very dogmatic about religious matters.
sentences.zh: 所以在宗教问题上，他非常非常教条。

sentences.en: He's a hardcore Puritan.
sentences.zh: 他是个顽固的清教徒。

sentences.en: This means that he gets on very well with the hardcore Calvinists, Puritans in Holland,
sentences.zh: 这意味着他与荷兰那些死硬的加尔文主义者和清教徒相处得很好，

sentences.en: but it alienates the mass of the people in the kind of the rebel cause in the Low Countries who aren't hardcore Calvinists.
sentences.zh: 但这却疏远了低地国家叛乱事业中大多数并非死硬加尔文主义者的普通民众。

sentences.en: They're what are called politique people who are essentially happy to live and let live to a degree.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为“务实派”（politique），本质上是乐于在某种程度上过一种“各行其是”的生活。

sentences.en: This isn't what Leicester's about at all.
sentences.zh: 莱斯特可完全不是这样的人。

sentences.en: Then in June 1586, he executes a Dutch commander who'd surrendered a fortress to the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1586年6月，他处决了一名向西班牙人投降的荷兰指挥官。

sentences.en: And again, this is not the kind of thing that the Dutch do.
sentences.zh: 同样，这不是荷兰人会做的那种事。

sentences.en: They think it's a terrible thing for Leicester to have done.
sentences.zh: 他们认为莱斯特做出这种事简直糟透了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And even while he's executing Dutch commanders for surrendering fortresses to the Spanish, Leicester himself is kind of sitting on his hands, refusing to go on the offensive.
sentences.zh: 甚至当他在处决那些向西班牙人投降堡垒的荷兰指挥官时，莱斯特自己却无所事事，拒绝发动进攻。

sentences.en: And even Sidney is starting to despair by the summer of 1586.
sentences.zh: 甚至到了1586年夏天，连西德尼也开始感到绝望。

sentences.en: And he writes to Leicester saying, the enemy stirs of every side and your side must not be idle.
sentences.zh: 他写信给莱斯特说，敌人四处蠢蠢欲动，你们这一方绝不能闲着。

sentences.en: For if it be, it quickly loses reputation.
sentences.zh: 因为如果无所作为，就会迅速失去声誉。

sentences.en: And of course, in the background, there is Elizabeth who is, you know, she's back to her old penny pinching ways.
sentences.zh: 当然，在背景里还有伊丽莎白，你知道的，她又回到了她那老一套吝啬的作风上。

sentences.en: She's refusing to send money to Sidney so that he can pay his garrison in Flushing.
sentences.zh: 她拒绝给西德尼寄钱，好让他支付驻扎在弗利辛恩的守军的军饷。

sentences.en: And again, Sidney's in despair.
sentences.zh: 西德尼再次陷入绝望。

sentences.en: If the queen pay not her soldiers, she must lose her garrisons.
sentences.zh: 如果女王不给她的士兵发军饷，她就必定会失去她的守军。

sentences.en: There is no doubt thereof.
sentences.zh: 这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: And so in short, everyone is incredibly annoyed with everyone else.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，每个人都对其他人感到无比恼火。

sentences.en: Elizabeth is quarrelling with Leicester.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白在和莱斯特争吵。

sentences.en: The English are quarrelling with the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 英国人在和荷兰人争吵。

sentences.en: Sidney's quarrelling with pretty much everyone else.
sentences.zh: 西德尼几乎在和所有人争吵。

sentences.en: He makes sure that people appreciate none of it is his fault.
sentences.zh: 他确保让大家明白，这绝不是他的错。

sentences.en: So he writes, no man living shall be able to say the fault is in me.
sentences.zh: 所以他写道，活着的任何人休想说错误在我。

sentences.en: I mean, I think you can perhaps see why Elizabeth finds him a bit annoying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想你大概能理解为什么伊丽莎白觉得他有点烦人。

sentences.en: But the thing is, this is all a surprise to me because I've always thought of Sir Philip Sidney as this tremendous hero.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这一切对我来说都是个惊喜，因为我一直把菲利普·西德尼爵士视为一个了不起的英雄。

sentences.en: You know, schools are named after him.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有以他名字命名的学校。

sentences.en: His name is written into the kind of annals of English patriotic legend.
sentences.zh: 他的名字被写进了英国爱国主义传奇的编年史中。

sentences.en: If they're just all squabbling with each other and behaving badly, why is he so admired?
sentences.zh: 如果他们只是在互相争吵、表现糟糕，为什么他会如此受人仰慕？

sentences.en: Because I think as with Byron, as with Che Guevara, he's going to die young and he's going to serve as a martyr for his cause.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为，就像拜伦一样，就像切·格瓦拉一样，他将会英年早逝，并将成为他所追求的事业的殉道者。

sentences.en: And that essentially is why Sidney becomes a kind of superstar to Protestant Europe.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是西德尼成为新教欧洲超级巨星的原因。

sentences.en: And so how does this happen?
sentences.zh: 那么这是怎么发生的呢？

sentences.en: So in September 1586, Leicester finally goes on the attack and he besieges and captures a Spanish-held town called Duysburg on the eastern flank of rebel-held territory.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1586年9月，莱斯特终于发起了进攻，他围攻并攻占了位于叛军控制领土东翼的一个由西班牙控制的名为杜伊斯堡（Duysburg）的城镇。

sentences.en: And if you're a fan of Dutch geography, it's in the province of Gelderland, which is to the southeast of the Zyde Zee.
sentences.zh: 如果你是荷兰地理的粉丝，它位于海尔德兰省，在须德海的东南方。

sentences.en: And Sidney rides out with Leicester.
sentences.zh: 西德尼和莱斯特一起骑马出征。

sentences.en: You know, hooray, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，万岁，太棒了。

sentences.en: He's got kind of feathers in his helmet.
sentences.zh: 他的头盔上插着羽毛。

sentences.en: He's got beautiful armour.
sentences.zh: 他穿着精美的盔甲。

sentences.en: He's having a brilliant time.
sentences.zh: 他过得好极了。

sentences.en: War at laSt.
sentences.zh: 终于开战了。

sentences.en: It seems to be going well.
sentences.zh: 事情似乎进展得很顺利。

sentences.en: And Leicester is buoyed by the sense that things are going his way.
sentences.zh: 由于感觉到事情正朝着有利于自己的方向发展，莱斯特深受鼓舞。

sentences.en: And so he moves on to his next target, which is a town called Zutphen.
sentences.zh: 于是他继续推进到他的下一个目标，一个叫做聚特芬（Zutphen）的城镇。

sentences.en: So the South Fen.
sentences.zh: 也就是南芬（South Fen）。

sentences.en: And Parma is very anxious to relieve this town.
sentences.zh: 帕尔马非常急于解救这座城镇。

sentences.en: And so he sends a force of 5,000 men to its rescue on the 22nd of September.
sentences.zh: 因此他在9月22日派遣了一支5000人的部队前往救援。

sentences.en: There's a big battle.
sentences.zh: 有一场大战。

sentences.en: There are lots of kind of heroic cavalry charges.
sentences.zh: 有许多英雄式的骑兵冲锋。

sentences.en: The English equit themselves very well.
sentences.zh: 英国人表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: However, they are unable to stop the Spanish from entering Zutphen.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们没能阻止西班牙人进入聚特芬。

sentences.en: And that basically is, that's the end of that.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这样，事情就到此为止了。

sentences.en: So it's a battle that I think no one would remember had Sir Philip Sidney not sustained a very serious wound in the course of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场我认为如果菲利普·西德尼爵士没有在其中身受重伤，就不会有人记住的战役。

sentences.en: And I said that there are these kind of dramatic cavalry charges.
sentences.zh: 我刚才说过有这些戏剧性的骑兵冲锋。

sentences.en: Sidney'd written in all of them.
sentences.zh: 西德尼参加了所有这些冲锋。

sentences.en: There are three in all.
sentences.zh: 总共有三次。

sentences.en: So the first time he'd, you know, drawn his sword, charged, hurrah, gone through the Spanish lines and then returned.
sentences.zh: 所以第一次他拔出剑，冲锋，万岁，冲过了西班牙人的防线，然后又返回。

sentences.en: The second time his horse had been shot from under him.
sentences.zh: 第二次他的马中弹倒地。

sentences.en: He got another horse.
sentences.zh: 他又换了一匹马。

sentences.en: Again, very gallant, very heroic.
sentences.zh: 同样非常勇敢，非常英雄。

sentences.en: The third time, again, he'd ridden through the enemy lines.
sentences.zh: 第三次，他又一次冲过了敌人的防线。

sentences.en: But then when he's turning to ride back to the English positions, he gets hit above his left knee by a musket ball.
sentences.zh: 但随后当他转身准备骑回英军阵地时，他的左膝上方被一颗火枪弹击中了。

sentences.en: And as Lester wrote in appalled tones later, it was a very dangerous wound.
sentences.zh: 正如莱斯特后来以震惊的口吻所写的那样，这是一处非常危险的伤口。

sentences.en: So Lester is very anxious for his nephew and his heir, of course, puts him in a barge, has him carried down the river to Arnhem, 20 miles south of Zutphen.
sentences.zh: 因此莱斯特非常担心他的侄子——当然也是他的继承人，把他放进一艘驳船里，顺流而下运到位于聚特芬以南20英里的阿纳姆（Arnhem）。

sentences.en: And in Arnhem, surgeons operate on the wound.
sentences.zh: 在阿纳姆，外科医生对伤口进行了手术。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, their attempt to extract the bullet only makes things worse.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，他们试图取出子弹的尝试反而让情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: And gangrene sets in.
sentences.zh: 坏疽开始蔓延。

sentences.en: And to quote, Sir Philip presently gave this severe doom upon himself that it was inward mortification and a welcome messenger of death.
sentences.zh: 引用当时的记载，菲利普爵士当即为自己作出了严厉的宣告，认为这是体内坏死，也是死亡的欢迎使者。

sentences.en: And sure enough, on the afternoon of the 17th of October, 1586, Sir Philip Sidney died at the tender age of 31.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，在1586年10月17日下午，菲利普·西德尼爵士在31岁的年轻大好年华去世了。

sentences.en: And it's a wretched, unhappy end, rather like Byron's end was wretched and unhappy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个凄惨而不幸的结局，就像拜伦的结局一样凄惨而不幸。

sentences.en: And in his dying hours, Sir Philip Sidney mourned that all things in my former life have been vain, vain, vain.
sentences.zh: 在他生命的最后时刻，菲利普·西德尼爵士哀叹道，我过去生命中的一切都是虚妄，虚妄，虚妄。

sentences.en: But this is not how his uncle, the Earl of Leicester, sees it.
sentences.zh: 但他的叔叔莱斯特伯爵可不这么看。

sentences.en: And Leicester may have been irascible, incompetent, arrogant.
sentences.zh: 莱斯特或许脾气暴躁、无能、傲慢。

sentences.en: But one thing he does know is how to create a martyr.
sentences.zh: 但他有一件事确实懂，那就是如何塑造一个殉道者。

sentences.en: And so Leicester ensures that Sidney's funeral cortege is very slow, very sombre, very stately.
sentences.zh: 因此，莱斯特确保西德尼的葬礼队伍非常缓慢、凝重而庄严。

sentences.en: And it processes from Arnhem to the sea and thence to London.
sentences.zh: 它从阿纳姆行进到海边，然后前往伦敦。

sentences.en: And in London, his coffin is carried to St. Paul's Cathedral by 14 men.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦，他的棺材由14名男子抬进圣保罗大教堂。

sentences.en: He's accompanied by the Lord Mayor, by 300 Londoners in full armour, and by a page riding Sidney's war horse, trailing a broken lance.
sentences.zh: 随行的有伦敦市长、300名身穿全套盔甲的伦敦市民，以及一名骑着西德尼战马、拖着断枪的随从页童。

sentences.en: So shades, perhaps, of the funeral of JFK.
sentences.zh: 这或许让人联想到约翰·F·肯尼迪的葬礼的影子。

sentences.en: And the streets were so thronged with people that the mourners had scarce room to pass.
sentences.zh: 街道上挤满了人，以至于哀悼者几乎没有地方通过。

sentences.en: And so in death, Sidney becomes what he had yearned to be all his life, a hero to every English Protestant and indeed to every Protestant in Christendom.
sentences.zh: 所以在死后，西德尼成为了他一生都渴望成为的人——每一个英国新教徒乃至整个基督教世界每一个新教徒心中的英雄。

sentences.en: And for Elizabeth and her PR team, her propaganda team, this must be a tremendous coup.
sentences.zh: 对于伊丽莎白和她的公关团队、她的宣传团队来说，这必定是一次巨大的成功。

sentences.en: Because it happens at precisely the point when it looks as though the storm clouds of war are moving over the English Channel towards their own beloved country.
sentences.zh: 因为这件事发生在一个精确的时刻，当时战争的乌云似乎正掠过英吉利海峡，朝他们自己心爱的国家压过来。

sentences.en: They're about to break.
sentences.zh: 它们即将爆发。

sentences.en: They are about to break, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 它们就要爆发了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, all of this has been building and building over the episodes of this series over the last few years.
sentences.zh: 因为我的意思是，所有这一切在过去几年这个系列的各集节目中一直在不断累积。

sentences.en: And the storm is, what is it?
sentences.zh: 而这场风暴是什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, is it pouring with rain over the dikes of the Low Countries?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是在低地国家的堤坝上倾盆大雨吗？

sentences.en: Surely there must be some metaphor you can employ here, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你在这里肯定能用上某种隐喻。

sentences.en: Yes, the storm is breaking over the dikes of the Low Countries and the rumbling of thunder can be heard on the south coast of England.
sentences.zh: 是的，风暴正在低地国家的堤坝上爆发，英格兰南海岸可以听到隆隆的雷声。

sentences.en: I think that's definitely the way to frame it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是构建它的方式。

sentences.en: But, of course, even as these war clouds are building, war is brewing as well amid the shadows.
sentences.zh: 但当然，正当这些战争阴云密布之时，战争也在阴影中酝酿。

sentences.en: And so in our next and final episode, we will be returning to that dimension of shadow, to a world of secrets and of spies and conspiracies.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们的下一集也是最后一集里，我们将回到那个充满阴影的维度，回到一个充满秘密、间谍和阴谋的世界。

sentences.en: And in particular, we will be tracking someone who has been absolutely central to this series, but who until now has been a largely offstage presence.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们将追踪某个人，她一直是本系列的核心，但直到现在基本上都处于舞台背后。

sentences.en: And Dominic, a personal favourite of yours, one of your great heroines,
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这是你的个人最爱，你伟大的女英雄之一，

sentences.en: someone who in all kinds of ways actually was the precise opposite of Sir Philip Sidney.
sentences.zh: 一个在各方面实际上都与菲利普·西德尼爵士截然相反的人。

sentences.en: So she's a woman, not a man, a Catholic, not a Protestant, and she's an ageing prisoner, not a youthful, dashing courtier.
sentences.zh: 所以她是个女人，而不是男人；是个天主教徒，而不是新教徒；她是一个日渐衰老的囚徒，而不是一个年轻潇洒的朝臣。

sentences.en: And we are talking, of course, about Mary, Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的当然是苏格兰女王玛丽。

sentences.en: Mary, Queen of Scots, and her appointment with the executioner, all to come in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽以及她与行刑者的会面，这一切都将在下一集中呈现。

sentences.en: Now, if you're a member of the Rest is History Club, if you're a member of our own expeditionary force to bring the gospel of history to the Low Countries,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你是“历史其余部分”俱乐部的成员，如果你是我们远征军的成员，致力于将历史的福音带给低地国家，

sentences.en: then you'll be able to hear that episode right now.
sentences.zh: 那么你现在就能听到那一集了。

sentences.en: And if you want to join them, if you want to join us in the dykes and whatever they are, the polders of the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 如果你想加入他们，如果你想和我们一起前往堤坝，或者荷兰的什么地方，那些圩田。

sentences.en: Love a polder.
sentences.zh: 我爱圩田。

sentences.en: If you want to join us, then head to therestishistory.com and sign up.
sentences.zh: 如果你想加入我们，那就前往 therestishistory.com 并注册。

sentences.en: And that is, of course, the only way that you'll be able to get this cornucopia of unbelievable benefits.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是你获得这取之不尽的令人难以置信的好处的唯一途径。

sentences.en: The other thing you probably want to do, this is a revelation, I imagine, to a lot of listeners, something I've never heard before.
sentences.zh: 你可能想做的另一件事是——我想这对许多听众来说是一个启发，是我从未听过的事情。

sentences.en: But we have a free newsletter with all kinds of incredible literary treats.
sentences.zh: 我们有一份免费的时事通讯，里面包含各种不可思议的文学精选。

sentences.en: So there are interviews and there are articles and there are book extracts and all kinds of fun things that you can't get anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 里面有采访、文章、书籍节选以及你在其他地方找不到的各种有趣内容。

sentences.en: And again, you go to our website, you sign up, and then you get this every week and you will be beside yourself.
sentences.zh: 同样的，你访问我们的网站，注册，然后你每周都会收到这个，你会兴奋得无以复加。

sentences.en: It's genuinely life-changing.
sentences.zh: 这真的能改变生活。

sentences.en: So on that bombshell, we will be back next time with Mary, Queen of Scots.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，我们下期将带着苏格兰女王玛丽回归。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。
